title: Chicken, NS as part, grilled with sauce, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide. This version uses boneless chicken breast grilled with a flavorful sauce. The skin is left on and eaten, adding taste and beneficial fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken meat is rich in protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.
Grilling preserves most nutrients while imparting a characteristic smoky aroma.
Chicken can be raised in various systems: free‑range, intensive, and organic.
Chicken skin contains monounsaturated fats and vitamin E.
There are many sauces for chicken: barbecue, teriyaki, honey‑mustard, and more.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Chicken breast provides about 31 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low fat (without skin)
items.content: Removing the skin makes chicken a low‑calorie source of energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken is a good source of niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are involved in metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains phosphorus, selenium, and zinc – important for immune function.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The combination of high protein and moderate fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked chicken can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter.

items.title: Sodium in sauces
items.content: Prepared sauces are often high in salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Fat in skin
items.content: Skin increases calorie count and saturated fat, which may be undesirable on low‑fat diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken can be enjoyed hot or cold, sliced into salads, used in sandwiches, incorporated into Asian dishes, or served with vegetable and grain sides.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked chicken in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions – up to 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before eating.
